results.title: Truncating the prime factorization of a binomial coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Then $\prod_{p=0}^{r} p^{v_p(\binom{N}{r})} = \binom{N}{r}$, where $v_p(m)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $m$ (zero when $p$ is not prime).

results.title: Prime-counting bound for binomial coefficients without large prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < N$ and $r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le N^{\pi(r)}$, where $\pi(r)$ is the number of primes $p \le r$.

results.title: Elementary power bound for binomial coefficients without large prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < N$ and $2 \le r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le N^{r-1}$.

results.title: Half-exponent bound for binomial coefficients without large prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < N$ and $r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le N^{\lfloor r/2 \rfloor + 1}$.

results.title: Three-eighths exponent bound for binomial coefficients without large prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < N$ and $38 \le r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le N^{\lfloor 3r/8 \rfloor}$.

results.title: Erdős root-layer bound for binomial coefficients without large prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < N$ and $r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Write $P(m)$ for the product of all primes $p \le m$ and let $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le \prod_{k=1}^{L} P(\lfloor N^{1/k} \rfloor)$.

results.title: Erdős layer bound for binomial coefficients without large prime factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < N$ and $r \le N$ be natural numbers such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Write $P(m)$ for the product of all primes $p \le m$ and let $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le \prod_{k=1}^{L} a_k$, where $a_1 = P(r)$ and $a_k = P(\lfloor N^{1/k} \rfloor)$ for $k \ge 2$.

results.title: Erdős layer bound with a one-third first layer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N \ge 6$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $2r \le N$ (hence $r \le N$) such that every prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ is at most $r$. Write $P(m)$ for the product of all primes $p \le m$ and let $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$. Then $\binom{N}{r} \le \prod_{k=1}^{L} a_k$, where $a_1 = P(\lfloor N/3 \rfloor)$ and $a_k = P(\lfloor N^{1/k} \rfloor)$ for $k \ge 2$.

results.title: Farey set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Farey set $F_n$ of order $n$ is the finite set of rationals $a/d$ with $a$ and $d$ natural numbers, $1 \le d \le n$ and $0 \le a \le d$.

results.title: Farey sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Farey sequence of order $n$ is the list of the elements of the Farey set $F_n$ in increasing order.

results.title: Membership in the Farey set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a rational number $q$, $q$ belongs to the Farey set $F_n$ of order $n$ if and only if $0 \le q \le 1$ and the denominator of $q$ in lowest terms is at most $n$.

results.title: Farey sets grow with the order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $m \le n$ are natural numbers, then every element of the Farey set $F_m$ belongs to $F_n$, that is, $F_m \subseteq F_n$.

results.title: Farey neighbors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, rationals $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$ when both lie in the Farey set $F_n$, $x < y$, and no element $z$ of $F_n$ satisfies $x < z < y$.

results.title: Mediant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For rational numbers $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ written in lowest terms with $b, d > 0$, the mediant of $x$ and $y$ is the rational number $(a + c)/(b + d)$.

results.title: Farey neighbors have denominator sum exceeding the order
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F_n$ be the Farey set of order $n$. If $x < y$ are neighbors in $F_n$, meaning that $x, y \in F_n$ and no element of $F_n$ lies strictly between them, then the denominators $b$ of $x$ and $d$ of $y$ in lowest terms satisfy $b + d > n$.

results.title: Determinant one and large denominator sum give Farey neighbors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ be elements of the Farey set $F_n$, written in lowest terms with $b, d > 0$. If $bc = ad + 1$ and $n < b + d$, then $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$.

results.title: Consecutive Farey fractions have determinant one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. If $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$, written in lowest terms as $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ with $b, d > 0$, then $bc = ad + 1$.

results.title: Arithmetic characterization of Farey neighbors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ be elements of the Farey set $F_n$, written in lowest terms with $b, d > 0$. Then $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$ if and only if $bc = ad + 1$ and $n < b + d$.

results.title: The mediant of Farey neighbors is not in the Farey set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. If $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$, then the mediant of $x$ and $y$ does not belong to the Farey set $F_n$.

results.title: Mediants that enter the next Farey set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x$ and $y$ be Farey neighbors of order $n$ whose denominators in lowest terms sum to $n + 1$. Then the mediant of $x$ and $y$ belongs to the Farey set $F_{n+1}$ and does not belong to $F_n$.

results.title: Mediants generate the next Farey set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. A rational number $q$ belongs to the Farey set $F_{n+1}$ if and only if $q$ belongs to $F_n$, or there are Farey neighbors $x$ and $y$ of order $n$ whose denominators in lowest terms sum to $n + 1$ such that $q$ is the mediant of $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Weighted forward shift of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For a weight sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, the weighted forward shift of $x$ is the sequence $y$ with $y_0 = 0$ and $y_{n+1} = w_n x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Weighted backward shift of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For weights $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, the weighted backward shift of $x$ is the sequence whose term at index $i$ is $\overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$.

results.title: Weighted forward shift at index zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For all weights $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and every sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, the term at index $0$ of the weighted forward shift of $x$ is $0$.

results.title: Weighted forward shift operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$. The weighted forward shift with weights $w$ is the bounded operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ obtained by first applying the diagonal operator $x \mapsto (w_n x_n)_{n}$ and then the unilateral forward shift $(x_0, x_1, \dots) \mapsto (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$.

results.title: Weighted backward shift on basis vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and write $e_n$ for the $n$-th standard basis vector of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $n$, the weighted backward shift $B_w$ satisfies $B_w e_{n+1} = \overline{w_n}\, e_n$.

results.title: Uniform weight bounds bound the weighted shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If $C$ is a real number with $|w_n| \le C$ for every $n$, then the operator norm of $S_w$ is at most $C$.

results.title: Operator norm of a weighted shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has operator norm $\|S_w\| = \sup_n |w_n|$.

results.title: Adjoint of the weighted shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The adjoint of the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, is the weighted backward shift $B_w$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$; that is, $S_w^* = B_w$.

results.title: Norm of the weighted backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The weighted backward shift $B_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$, has operator norm $\|B_w\| = \sup_n |w_n|$.

results.title: Norm bound for weighted shift images
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the weighted forward shift $S_w$, viewed as a linear map, satisfies $\|S_w x\| \le \left(\sup_n |w_n|\right) \|x\|$.

results.title: Norm bound for the weighted backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$, and let $B_w$ be the weighted backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. Then $\|B_w x\| \le (\sup_n |w_n|)\, \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The weighted backward shift after the forward shift is diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$, and on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift, $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, and $B_w$ the weighted backward shift, $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. Then $(B_w S_w x)_i = |w_i|^2 x_i$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and…

results.title: Forward-after-backward weighted shift is diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and let $S_w$ and $B_w$ be the weighted forward and backward shifts on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the composite $S_w B_w$ satisfies $(S_w B_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w B_w x)_i = |w_{i-1}|^2 x_i$ for every $i \ge 1$.

results.title: The weighted backward shift is a left inverse for unimodular weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $|w_n| = 1$ for every $n$. On $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift, $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, and $B_w$ the weighted backward shift, $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. Then $B_w S_w$ is the identity operator.

results.title: Weighted shifts with nonzero weights are injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $w_n \neq 0$ for every $n$. Then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, is injective.

results.title: A vanishing weight makes the weighted shift non-injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. If $w_n = 0$ for some $n$, then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is not injective.

results.title: Weighted shifts with unimodular weights preserve norms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with $|w_n| = 1$ for every $n$. Then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, satisfies $\|S_w x\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: Isometric weighted shifts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(S_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w x)_{n+1} = w_n x_n$, is an isometry if and only if $|w_n| = 1$ for every $n$.

results.title: The weighted forward shift with unit weights is the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The weighted forward shift operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ whose weights are all equal to $1$ is the unilateral forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: Unit weights give the plain backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. With every weight equal to $1$, the weighted backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the canonical backward shift.

results.title: Truncated weights
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For a sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the truncation of $w$ after $N$ coordinates is the sequence $w^{(N)}$ with $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$ for $n < N$ and $w^{(N)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge N$.

results.title: Truncated weights agree with the weights below the cutoff
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, and let $N, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n < N$. Then the truncation $w^{(N)}$ of $w$ after $N$ coordinates (equal to $w_k$ for $k < N$ and to $0$ for $k \ge N$) satisfies $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$.

results.title: Truncated weights vanish from the cutoff on
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$, and let $N, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge N$. Then the truncation $w^{(N)}$ of $w$ after $N$ coordinates (equal to $w_k$ for $k < N$ and to $0$ for $k \ge N$) satisfies $w^{(N)}_n = 0$.

results.title: Truncated weights are bounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded, that is, $|w_n| \le C$ for all $n$ for some constant $C$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. Then the truncation $w^{(N)}$ of $w$ after $N$ coordinates, given by $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$ for $n < N$ and $w^{(N)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge N$, is bounded as well.

results.title: Differences of bounded sequences are bounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w, v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded sequences, that is, there are constants $C$ and $D$ with $|w_n| \le C$ and $|v_n| \le D$ for all $n$. Then $w - v$ is bounded: there is a constant $E$ with $|w_n - v_n| \le E$ for all $n$.

results.title: Weighted shift of a difference of weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w, v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be sequences such that $w$, $v$ and $w - v$ are bounded. Writing $S_u$ for the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ with bounded weights $u$, sending $x$ to $(0, u_0 x_0, u_1 x_1, \dots)$, we have $S_{w - v} = S_w - S_v$.

results.caption: Theorem

For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ let $w^{(N)}$ be the truncation of $w$ after $N$ coordinates, with $w^{(N)}_n = w_n$ for $n < N$ and $w^{(N)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge N$, and for bounded weights $u$ let $S_u$ be the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, sending $x$ to…

results.title: Compactness criterion for weighted shifts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence of weights, that is, $|w_n| \le C$ for all $n$ for some constant $C$. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, which sends $x$ to $(0, w_0 x_0, w_1 x_1, \dots)$, is a compact operator if and only if $w_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Weighted shifts with eventually vanishing weights are compact
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence of weights, and suppose there is $N \in \mathbb{N}$ with $w_n = 0$ for all $n \ge N$. Then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, which sends $x$ to $(0, w_0 x_0, w_1 x_1, \dots)$, is a compact operator.

results.title: Banach–Mazur embedding theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every separable real Banach space $E$ admits a linear isometric embedding $e \colon E \to C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ into the space of continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$ with the supremum norm, such that the range of $e$ is closed.

results.title: Banach–Stone theorem for real scalars
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Hausdorff spaces, and let $C(X, \mathbb{R})$ and $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$ be the real Banach spaces of continuous real functions on them with the supremum norm. If there is a surjective linear isometry from $C(X, \mathbb{R})$ onto $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$, then $X$ and $Y$ are homeomorphic.

results.title: Bishop–Phelps theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with dual space $E^*$. The functionals that attain their norm on the closed unit ball, that is, the $f \in E^*$ such that $|f(x)| = \|f\|$ for some $x \in E$ with $\|x\| \le 1$, form a dense subset of $E^*$ in the norm topology.

results.title: Daugavet's theorem for compact operators
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C[0,1]$ be the real Banach space of continuous functions $[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with the supremum norm, and let $I$ be the identity operator on it. Every compact bounded linear operator $T : C[0,1] \to C[0,1]$ satisfies $\|I + T\| = 1 + \|T\|$, where the norms are operator norms.

results.title: Dvoretzky–Rogers theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space $E$ contains a series that converges unconditionally but not absolutely: there is a sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $E$ such that the rearranged series $\sum_n x_{\sigma(n)}$ converges for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{N}$, while $\sum_n \lVert x_n \rVert$ diverges.

results.title: Milman–Pettis theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $E^*$ be the space of continuous linear functionals on $E$. Then every continuous linear functional $\Phi$ on $E^*$ is evaluation at a point: there is $x \in E$ with $\Phi(f) = f(x)$ for every $f \in E^*$.

results.title: Banach–Saks theorem for uniformly convex spaces
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real Banach space and let $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $E$. Then there are a strictly increasing map $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a point $y \in E$ such that the Cesàro means $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{\varphi(i)}$ converge to $y$ in norm as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Multiway number partition instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A multiway number partition instance is a pair $(a, K)$ consisting of a list $a$ of natural numbers and a natural number $K$ (the number of parts).

results.title: Feasible multiway number partition instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(a, K)$ be a multiway number partition instance with $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{m-1})$. It is feasible when $K \ge 1$ and there is a map $f$ from $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ onto $\{0, \dots, K-1\}$ such that the sums $\sum_{j < m,\, f(j) = p} a_j$ for $p = 0, \dots, K-1$ are all equal. In other words, the entries of $a$, counted with repetition, can be split into $K$ nonempty parts with equal sums.

results.title: The MULTIWAY NUMBER PARTITION decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: MULTIWAY NUMBER PARTITION is the decision problem on bitstrings that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a multiway number partition instance $(a, K)$ that is feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to a multiway number partition instance are rejected.

results.title: One round of the DFA reachability search
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $\alpha$. The round sends a finite set $S$ of states of $M$ to the set consisting of the start state of $M$ and of every state that the transition function of $M$ takes some $s \in S$ to on some letter $a \in \alpha$.

results.title: Reachable states of a DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet whose set of states $\sigma$ is finite and has decidable equality. The reachable states of $M$ form the finite set obtained from the empty set by applying one round of the DFA reachability search for $M$ exactly $|\sigma|$ times, where $|\sigma|$ is the number of states of $M$.

results.title: A state is reachable exactly when some word leads to it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. A state $s$ of $M$ is in the set of reachable states of $M$ if and only if there is a word $w$ such that running $M$ on $w$ from its start state ends in $s$.

results.title: The start state is reachable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the start state of $M$ belongs to the reachable states of $M$.

results.title: Reachable states are closed under transitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet whose set of states is finite and has decidable equality. If a state $s$ of $M$ is reachable from the start state, then for every letter $a$ the state to which $M$ moves from $s$ on $a$ is also reachable from the start state.

results.title: The early-stopping search finds exactly the reachable states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. For every natural number $n$ at least the number of states of $M$, the early-stopping reachability search for $M$ from the empty set with at most $n$ rounds returns the set of reachable states of $M$.

results.title: Every state of the accessible part is reached
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Emptiness test for DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the emptiness test returns true exactly when none of the reachable states of $M$ is an accepting state.

results.title: The emptiness test decides emptiness of DFAs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. The emptiness test applied to $M$ returns true if and only if the language accepted by $M$ is empty.

results.title: Universality test for DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the universality test applied to $M$ is the emptiness test applied to the complement of $M$: the DFA with the same states, start state and transitions whose accepting states are the states that $M$ does not accept.

results.title: The universality test decides universality of DFAs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. The universality test applied to $M$ returns true if and only if $M$ accepts every word over the alphabet.

results.title: Correctness of the equivalence test for DFAs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be DFAs over the same finite alphabet, with finite state sets with decidable equality and decidable sets of accepting states. The equivalence test of $M$ and $N$ returns true if and only if $M$ and $N$ accept the same language.

results.title: Acceptance test for encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a word $w$ over $\alpha$, the acceptance test is the Boolean that is true exactly when the state reached by running $D$ on $w$ from its start state is in the list of accepting states of $D$.

results.title: Reachable states of an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the reachable states of $D$ form the list returned by the bounded reachability search on lists of states started at the start state of $D$, kept inside the states of $D$, in which the successors of a state $s$ are the states that the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ to on the letters of $D$, in the order of the letters.

results.title: Emptiness test for encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the emptiness test is the Boolean that is true exactly when no entry of the list of reachable states of $D$ is in the accepting list of $D$.

results.title: Coded pairs of states of two encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For encoded DFAs $D$ and $E$ over the same alphabet, code a pair $(s, t)$ of natural numbers by its image $\langle s, t \rangle \in \mathbb{N}$ under Mathlib's pairing function. This is the list of the numbers $\langle s, t \rangle$ with $s$ running over the states of $D$ in their listed order and, for each $s$, $t$ running over the states of $E$ in their listed order.

results.title: Successors of a pair of states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ and $E$ be encoded DFAs over the same alphabet, and let $p \in \mathbb{N}$ code the pair of states $(s, t)$ under the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. The successors of $p$ form the list that has, for each letter $a$ in the letters of $D$ followed by the letters of $E$, the code of the pair made of the step of $D$ from $s$ on $a$ and the step of $E$ from $t$ on $a$.

results.title: Reachable pairs of states of two encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition

The reachable pairs of $D$ and $E$ form the list returned by the bounded reachability search on lists of states started at $\langle s_D, s_E \rangle$, where $s_D$ and $s_E$ are the start states of $D$ and $E$, kept inside the list of coded…

results.title: Equivalence test for encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ and $E$ be encoded DFAs over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality. The equivalence test of $D$ and $E$ is the Boolean that is true exactly when, for every entry $p$ of the list of reachable pairs of states of $D$ and $E$, writing $p = \langle s, t \rangle$ with Mathlib's pairing function, $s$ is in the accepting list of $D$ if and only if $t$ is in the accepting list of $E$.

results.title: Universality test for encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the universality test is the Boolean that is true exactly when every entry of the list of reachable states of $D$ is in the accepting list of $D$.

results.title: An encoded DFA on its listed states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$, this is the DFA whose set of states is the finite set of states of $D$ (its start state and the targets of its listed transitions), whose start state is the start state of $D$, whose transition function is that of $D$ restricted to these states, and whose accepting states are those in the accepting list of $D$.

results.title: A long accepted word makes the language of an encoded DFA infinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA and let $N$ be the length of the list of states of $D$. If $D$ accepts a word of length at least $N$, then the language of $D$ is infinite.

results.title: Accepted words of length between the number of listed states and twice it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, and let $N$ be the length of its list of states. For every natural number $n$ and every word $w$ of length $n$ in the language of $D$ with $N \le n$, the language of $D$ contains a word $v$ whose length $|v|$ satisfies $N \le |v| < 2N$.

results.title: Words of a given length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ given with an enumeration of its letters and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the words of length $n$ over $\alpha$: starting from the list whose only entry is the empty word, it replaces $n$ times each word $w$ of the current list by the words $a w$ for the letters $a$ of $\alpha$, in their enumeration order.

results.title: Infiniteness test for encoded DFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA over a finite alphabet and let $N$ be the length of its list of states. The infiniteness test is the Boolean that is true exactly when the language of $D$ contains a word $w$ with $N \le |w| < 2N$; it checks every word of each length $N + i$ with $0 \le i < N$.

results.title: Correctness of the infiniteness test for encoded DFAs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded DFA $D$ over a finite alphabet, the infiniteness test returns true on $D$ if and only if the language of $D$ is infinite.

results.title: Acceptance for DFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(D, w)$ of an encoded DFA $D$ over $\alpha$ and a word $w$ over $\alpha$ that $w$ belongs to the language of $D$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $A_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.

results.title: Emptiness of DFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ that its language is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $E_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.

results.title: Equivalence of DFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair of encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ that their languages are equal is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{EQ}_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.

results.title: Universality of DFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ that its language is the set of all words over $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{ALL}_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.

results.title: Infiniteness of DFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite alphabet $\alpha$, given with an enumeration of its letters, decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ that its language is infinite is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{INFINITE}_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.

results.title: Flag bit of a machine state
results.caption: Class
results.summary: A flag on a type $\sigma$ of machine states consists of a map $\mathrm{tag} : \mathrm{Bool} \to \sigma$ that stores a bit in a state and a map $\mathrm{untag} : \sigma \to \mathrm{Bool}$ that reads it back, such that $\mathrm{untag}(\mathrm{tag}(\beta)) = \beta$ for every bit $\beta$. The program primitives use it to branch on whether a pop found a symbol.

results.title: A halted run stays halted
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \sigma \to \mathrm{Option}\,\sigma$ be a partial step function and let $\hat f$ be its lift to $\mathrm{Option}\,\sigma$, which sends $\mathrm{none}$ to $\mathrm{none}$ and $\mathrm{some}\,x$ to $f(x)$. Then $\hat f^{\,n}(\mathrm{none}) = \mathrm{none}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Exact-length runs of a TM2 machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a TM2 machine, given by a statement for each label, and let $c$ and $d$ be configurations. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $M$ runs from $c$ to $d$ in exactly $n$ steps when applying the step function of $M$ $n$ times, starting at $c$, is defined at every step (no configuration before the last one has halted) and ends at $d$.

results.title: A single step executes the statement at the current label
results.caption: Theorem

If executing the statement $M(l)$ from state $v$ and stacks $S$ yields $d$, then $M$ runs in exactly one step from the configuration with label $l$, state $v$ and stacks $S$ to $d$.

results.title: Unary counter
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The unary counter with unit symbol $u$ and value $n \in \mathbb{N}$ is the list $u^n$ consisting of exactly $n$ copies of $u$.

results.title: Counter increment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a stack $k$, a symbol $u$ of stack $k$ (the unit of a unary counter) and a label $\ell$, this statement pushes $u$ onto stack $k$ and then goes to label $\ell$.

results.title: Decrement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a stack $k$ and labels $\ell_0$ and $\ell_+$, this machine statement pops stack $k$, stores in the state whether a symbol was popped, and goes to $\ell_+$ if a symbol was popped and to $\ell_0$ if stack $k$ was empty.

results.title: Pushing symbols onto several stacks
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Adding units to target stacks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of pairs $(j, x)$ of a stack $j$ and a symbol $x$ of stack $j$, let $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $S$ be stacks. The resulting stacks are as follows: if $(k, x)$ is the first pair in $ps$ whose stack is $k$, stack $k$ holds $i$ copies of $x$ followed by $S_k$ (so the copies are on top); if no pair in $ps$ has stack $k$, stack $k$ holds $S_k$.

results.title: Termwise bound on a sum of consecutive values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c, i, j \in \mathbb{N}$. If $f(t) \le c$ for every $t$ with $i \le t < i + j$, then $\mathrm{sumFrom}(f, i, j) = f(i) + f(i+1) + \dots + f(i+j-1)$ is at most $j \cdot c$.

results.title: Height-indexed 2-3 trees
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of keys, the 2-3 trees over $\alpha$ indexed by height are generated as follows. The leaf is a tree of height $0$ and stores no key. For a natural number $h$, a key $a$ and trees $l$, $r$ of height $h$, the 2-node with separator $a$ and children $l$, $r$ is a tree of height $h + 1$. For a natural number $h$, keys $a$, $b$ and trees $l$, $m$, $r$ of height $h$, the 3-node with separators $a$, $b$…

results.title: Insertion results for 2-3 trees
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a natural number $h$, an insertion result at height $h$ is either a 2-3 tree over $\alpha$ of height $h$, or a split: two 2-3 trees $l$ and $r$ over $\alpha$ of height $h$ together with a promoted key $k \in \alpha$.

results.title: Height of a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The height of a 2-3 tree is computed along its leftmost spine: a leaf has height $0$, and a 2-node or a 3-node has height one more than the height of its leftmost child.

results.title: Computed height equals the height index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every 2-3 tree $t$ with height index $h$, the height of $t$ computed along its leftmost spine equals $h$.

results.title: Balance invariant for 2-3 trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A leaf is balanced, and a node is balanced when all of its subtrees are balanced and have the same computed height, where the computed height of a tree is the length of its leftmost path from the root down to a leaf. Hence all leaves of a balanced tree lie at the same depth.

results.title: Every height-indexed 2-3 tree is balanced
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every height $h$, every 2-3 tree of height $h$ satisfies the balance invariant: at every node, the subtrees are balanced and have equal computed heights.

results.title: Membership in a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A key $x$ is a member of a 2-3 tree when it is one of the separator keys stored at its nodes: nothing is a member of a leaf; $x$ is a member of a 2-node with key $a$ and children $l, r$ when it is a member of $l$, equals $a$, or is a member of $r$; and $x$ is a member of a 3-node with keys $a, b$ and children $l, m, r$ when it is a member of $l$, equals $a$, is a member of $m$, equals $b$, or is a member of $r$.

results.title: Predicate on all keys of a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a predicate $p$ on keys and a 2-3 tree $t$, $\mathrm{All}_p(t)$ states that every separator key stored at a node of $t$ satisfies $p$: it is true at a leaf, and at a node it requires $p$ of each key of the node and $\mathrm{All}_p$ of each of its subtrees.

results.title: All-keys predicate agrees with membership on 2-3 trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on keys and every 2-3 tree $t$ of height $h$, the recursive predicate requiring $p$ at every key stored at a node of $t$ holds if and only if $p(x)$ holds for every member $x$ of $t$, where $x$ is a member of $t$ when it equals one of the keys stored at some node of $t$.

results.title: Ordering invariant for 2-3 trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$. The leaf is ordered. A 2-node with separator $a$ and children $l$, $r$ is ordered when $l$ and $r$ are ordered, $y < a$ for every key $y$ stored in $l$, and $a < y$ for every key $y$ stored in $r$. A 3-node with separators $a$, $b$ and children $l$, $m$, $r$ is ordered when $l$, $m$ and $r$ are ordered, $a < b$, $y < a$ for every key $y$ stored in $l$, $a < y$ and $y < b$…

results.title: Accumulated inorder traversal of a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a 2-3 tree $t$ and a list $s$, the accumulated traversal $F(t, s)$ is defined by recursion on $t$: for a leaf, $F(t, s) = s$; for a 2-node with key $a$ and children $l, r$, $F(t, s)$ is $F(l, s')$ where $s'$ is $a$ prepended to $F(r, s)$; for a 3-node with keys $a, b$ and children $l, m, r$, $F(t, s)$ is $F(l, s')$ where $s'$ is $a$ prepended to $F(m, s'')$ and $s''$ is $b$ prepended to $F(r, s)$.

results.title: Inorder traversal of a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The flattening of a 2-3 tree $t$ is the accumulated inorder traversal of $t$ onto the empty list. Equivalently, the flattening of a leaf is empty; that of a 2-node with key $a$ and children $l, r$ is the flattening of $l$, then $a$, then the flattening of $r$; and that of a 3-node with keys $a, b$ and children $l, m, r$ is the flattening of $l$, then $a$, then the flattening of $m$, then $b$, then the flattening of…

results.title: The accumulated traversal appends the suffix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every 2-3 tree $t$ (of any height) and every list $s$, the accumulated inorder traversal of $t$ onto $s$ equals the flattening of $t$ followed by $s$.

results.title: The inorder traversal lists exactly the keys of a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every 2-3 tree $t$ of height $h$ and every key $x$, $x$ occurs in the inorder traversal of $t$ if and only if $x$ is a member of $t$, that is, one of the separator keys stored at its nodes.

results.title: All-keys predicate agrees with the flattening on 2-3 trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on keys and every 2-3 tree $t$ of height $h$, every key stored at a node of $t$ satisfies $p$ if and only if every element of the inorder flattening of $t$ satisfies $p$.

results.title: Inorder traversal of an ordered 2-3 tree is strictly increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every natural number $h$ and every ordered 2-3 tree $t$ over $\alpha$ of height $h$, the flattening (inorder traversal) of $t$ is strictly increasing: whenever a key $x$ occurs before a key $y$ in it, $x < y$.

results.title: The traversal of an ordered 2-3 tree has no duplicates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the keys are linearly ordered and a 2-3 tree $t$ (of any height) is ordered, then no key occurs twice in the flattening of $t$.

results.title: Search in a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, searching a 2-3 tree for a key $x$ returns false at a leaf. At a 2-node with key $a$, it searches the left subtree if $x < a$, otherwise the right subtree if $a < x$, and otherwise returns true. At a 3-node with keys $a$ and $b$, it searches the left subtree if $x < a$; otherwise, if $a < x$, it searches the middle subtree if $x < b$, otherwise the right subtree if $b < x$, and…

results.title: Search in an ordered 2-3 tree is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered and let $t$ be a 2-3 tree of height $h$ that satisfies the ordering invariant. Then searching $t$ for a key $x$ returns true if and only if $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $t$.

results.title: Insertion into a height-indexed 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Inserting a key $x$ into a 2-3 tree of height $h$ yields either a single tree of height $h$ or a split into two trees of height $h$ around a promoted key. Inserting into a leaf gives the split of two leaves around $x$. At a 2-node with key $a$, insertion recurses into the left child if $x < a$ and into the right child if $a < x$; a returned tree replaces that child, and a returned split around $k$ is absorbed by…

results.title: Insertion specification for 2-3 trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $t$ be a 2-3 tree of height $h$. An insertion result of height $h$ meets the specification for inserting $x$ into $t$ when the following holds. If it is a single tree $t'$ of height $h$, then $t'$ is ordered and its inorder traversal equals the ordered insertion of $x$ into the inorder traversal of $t$. If it is a split into trees $l$ and $r$ of height…

results.title: Correctness of 2-3 tree insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $t$ be an ordered 2-3 tree of height $h$. Then inserting $x$ into $t$ meets the insertion specification. If the insertion returns a single tree $t'$ of height $h$, then $t'$ is ordered and its inorder traversal is the ordered insertion of $x$ into the inorder traversal of $t$. If it returns a split into trees $l$ and $r$ of height $h$ around a promoted…

results.title: 2-3 trees of unspecified height
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$, a 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ is a pair $(h, t)$ of a natural number $h$ and a height-indexed 2-3 tree $t$ over $\alpha$ of height $h$.

results.title: Turning an insertion result into a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An insertion result at height $h$ becomes a 2-3 tree of unspecified height as follows: a tree $t$ of height $h$ gives $t$ itself, of height $h$, and a split into trees $l$, $r$ of height $h$ around a key $k$ gives the 2-node with separator $k$, left child $l$ and right child $r$, of height $h + 1$.

results.title: Empty 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The empty 2-3 tree is the root of height $0$ whose underlying tree is the leaf.

results.title: Inorder traversal of a 2-3 tree root
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The flattening of a 2-3 tree root is the flattening of its underlying tree, that is, the list of its keys in inorder.

results.title: Search in a rooted 2-3 tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, searching a root (a 2-3 tree packaged with its height) for a key $x$ returns the Boolean result of the 2-3 tree search for $x$ in the underlying height-indexed tree.

results.title: Ordering invariant for 2-3 trees of unspecified height
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$. A 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ is ordered when its underlying height-indexed 2-3 tree satisfies the ordering invariant.

results.title: Insertion into a 2-3 tree root
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: To insert a key $x$ into a root, that is, a 2-3 tree together with its height $h$, insert $x$ into the underlying tree. If this returns a single tree of height $h$, that tree is the new root, of height $h$. If it returns a split into trees $l$ and $r$ around a key $k$, the new root is the 2-node with key $k$ and children $l$ and $r$, of height $h + 1$.

results.title: The empty 2-3 tree is ordered
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type $\alpha$ with a relation $<$, the empty 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ (the leaf, of height $0$) satisfies the ordering invariant.

results.title: The stored height of a 2-3 tree root is its computed height
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every root $t$, that is, a 2-3 tree together with its height index, the height of the underlying tree computed along its leftmost spine equals the stored height of $t$.

results.title: Every rooted 2-3 tree is balanced
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every root, that is, a 2-3 tree packaged with its height, the underlying height-indexed tree satisfies the balance invariant.

results.title: Insertion preserves the ordering of 2-3 trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. If $t$ is an ordered 2-3 tree of unspecified height over $\alpha$ and $x \in \alpha$, then the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ is ordered.

results.title: Insertion into a 2-3 tree is ordered insertion into its traversal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered, let $t$ be an ordered 2-3 tree root and let $x$ be a key. Then the flattening of the root obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ equals the ordered insertion of $x$ into the flattening of $t$.

results.title: Keys after insertion into a 2-3 tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered and let $t$ be an ordered 2-3 tree root over $\alpha$. For all $x, y \in \alpha$, $y$ occurs in the inorder traversal of the root obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ if and only if $y = x$ or $y$ occurs in the inorder traversal of $t$.

results.title: Search in a rooted 2-3 tree is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered and let $t$ be a root (a 2-3 tree packaged with its height) whose underlying tree satisfies the ordering invariant. Then searching $t$ for a key $x$ returns true if and only if $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $t$.

results.title: Insertion raises the height of a 2-3 tree by at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For linearly ordered keys, every key $x$ and every 2-3 tree root $t$, the stored height of the root obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ is at most the stored height of $t$ plus one.

results.title: Building a 2-3 tree from a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For linearly ordered keys, the 2-3 tree root built from a list is defined by recursion: the empty list gives the empty 2-3 tree, and a list with head $x$ and tail $xs$ gives the result of inserting $x$ into the root built from $xs$. Thus the elements are inserted into the empty tree from the last to the first.

results.title: Building a 2-3 tree from a list gives an ordered tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, the 2-3 tree of unspecified height built from $L$, by inserting the elements of $L$ from right to left into the empty tree, is ordered.

results.title: Keys of a 2-3 tree built from a list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered. For every list $L$ over $\alpha$ and every $x \in \alpha$, $x$ occurs in the inorder traversal of the 2-3 tree built from $L$ (by inserting its elements from right to left into the empty tree) if and only if $x$ occurs in $L$.

results.title: CRC encoder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $g$ be a polynomial over $F$ (the generator), and let $r$ be the degree of $g$ (with $r = 0$ when $g = 0$). The CRC encoding of a polynomial $m$ over $F$ (the message) is $m X^r - (m X^r \bmod g)$: the message shifted up by $r$ positions, minus the remainder of the shifted message modulo $g$.

results.title: CRC encoding in characteristic 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic 2 (for example $\mathbb{F}_2$), let $g$ and $m$ be polynomials over $F$, and let $r$ be the degree of $g$ (with $r = 0$ when $g = 0$). Then the CRC encoding of $m$ with generator $g$ equals $m X^r + (m X^r \bmod g)$: the encoder appends the remainder to the shifted message.

results.title: CRC codewords are multiples of the generator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field. For all polynomials $g$ and $m$ over $F$, the polynomial $g$ divides the CRC encoding of $m$ with generator $g$.

results.title: CRC encoding is systematic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $g \ne 0$ a polynomial over $F$ of degree $r$. For every message polynomial $m$ over $F$ and every natural number $i$, the coefficient of $X^{i+r}$ in the CRC encoding of $m$ with generator $g$ equals the coefficient of $X^i$ in $m$.

results.title: CRC detection criterion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $g$, $m$ and $e$ be polynomials over $F$, and let $c$ be the CRC encoding of $m$ with generator $g$. Then $g$ divides $c + e$ if and only if $g$ divides $e$: a codeword plus an error pattern passes the check exactly when $g$ divides the error.

results.title: Single-symbol errors are detected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $g$ a polynomial over $F$ with at least two nonzero coefficients. Then $g$ does not divide $a X^i$ for any nonzero $a \in F$ and any natural number $i$.

results.title: Burst errors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $L$ a natural number. A polynomial $e$ over $F$ is a burst of length at most $L$ when $e = X^i b$ for some natural number $i$ and some polynomial $b$ over $F$ with $b(0) \ne 0$ and $\deg b < L$. Then the nonzero coefficients of $e$ lie in positions $i, \dots, i + L - 1$, the first one nonzero.

results.title: Errors confined to a window are bursts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $e \ne 0$ be a polynomial over $F$, and let $i$ and $L$ be natural numbers. If every $j$ for which the coefficient of $X^j$ in $e$ is nonzero satisfies $i \le j < i + L$, then $e$ is a burst of length at most $L$.

results.title: Short bursts are detected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $g$ be a polynomial over $F$ that is not divisible by $X$, and let $L$ be a natural number with $L \le \deg g$. If a polynomial $e$ over $F$ is a burst of length at most $L$, then $g$ does not divide $e$.

results.title: CRC error-detection guarantee
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $g$ be a polynomial over $F$ with at least two nonzero coefficients that is not divisible by $X$, let $m$ be a polynomial over $F$, and let $c$ be the CRC encoding of $m$ with generator $g$. Then $g$ does not divide $c + aX^i$ for any nonzero $a \in F$ and any natural number $i$, and $g$ does not divide $c + e$ for any polynomial $e$ over $F$ that is a burst of length at most $\deg g$.
